speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities in more detail, and when did it first appear relative to your fever and headache?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The timeline of a facial rash appearing days after prodromal symptoms and spreading to the trunk is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). I need to confirm the characteristic appearance of the facial rash to be certain.

Can you describe the pattern of the rash on her face, specifically does it look like "slapped cheeks"?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The "slapped cheek" appearance sparing the perioral area, followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities after a viral prodrome, is classic for Parvovirus B19 infection. I am confident in this clinical presentation.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
